chunks: What Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn Mahzīyār, who said:

Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام wrote to him, and I myself read his letter to him on the road to Makkah. He said: What I have made obligatory in this year of mine—and this is the year two hundred and twenty only—is for a certain reason among the reasons; I dislike explaining the entire reason for fear of its spreading, and I shall explain the remainder of it to you, if Allah wills. Indeed my followers—may Allah set them aright—or some of them, have fallen short regarding what is obligatory upon them. I came to know that, and I wished to purify them and cleanse them by what I have enacted in this year of mine concerning the khums.

Allah, Exalted is He, said: “Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cleanse them, and pray for them; indeed your prayer is a comfort for them. And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing. Do they not know that Allah is He who accepts repentance from His servants and takes charities, and that Allah is the Oft-Returning, the Merciful? And say: Act, for Allah will see your deeds, and His Messenger, and the believers; and you shall be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the seen, and He will inform you of what you used to do.”

And I did not make that obligatory upon them in every year, nor do I make anything obligatory upon them except the zakat that Allah has made obligatory upon them. I have only made khums obligatory upon them in this year of mine regarding gold and silver upon which a year has passed. I did not make that obligatory upon them concerning goods, nor vessels, nor riding animals, nor servants, nor profit earned in trade, nor landed property—except for an estate whose matter I shall explain to you—as a lightening from me for my followers and as a favor from me upon them, because of what the ruler seizes from their wealth and because of what befalls them in their persons.

As for spoils and gains, they are obligatory upon them in every year. Allah, Exalted is He, said: “And know that whatever you gain of anything, then indeed for Allah is its fifth, and for the Messenger, and for the near of kin, and the orphans, and the needy, and the traveler, if you believe in Allah and what We sent down upon Our servant on the Day of Criterion, the day the two hosts met. And Allah is Powerful over all things.”

And spoils and gains—may Allah have mercy on you—are: the booty a man acquires, and the benefit he obtains, and a gift from a person that is of significant value, and an inheritance that is not expected from other than a father or a son, and the like of an enemy who is wiped out and his wealth is taken, and the like of wealth that is taken while its owner is unknown, and what has come to my followers from the wealth of the sinful Khurramiyyah. I have learned that great amounts of wealth have come to a group among my followers, so whoever has any of that with him should deliver it to my agent; and whoever is far away, at a great distance, should deliberately seek to deliver it, even after some time, for indeed the intention of the believer is better than his action.

As for what I make obligatory from estates and yields in every year, it is one-half of one-sixth upon one whose estate suffices for his maintenance. As for one whose estate does not suffice for his maintenance, then there is neither one-half of one-sixth nor anything else upon him.

We have fully treated what relates to this chapter in our major book, and we have explained the differing statements of our companions regarding the state of the ghaybah and how khums ought to be acted upon. We have clarified the sound view therein, what may validly be practiced, and added what is needed to be known regarding the manner of disposal in landed properties that are divided into that which belongs specifically to the Imam—namely the land of al-anfāl and others—and that in which he alone has authority of disposal, namely kharāj lands that were opened by force; and on what basis it is permissible for us to dispose of them. We also cited the reports that have come concerning that and pointed out what practice ought to be based upon. So whoever wishes to examine all of that should seek it all from there, if Allah, Exalted is He, wills.

key_terms.الزَّكَاةَ: the obligatory alms-tax already prescribed by Allah
key_terms.الْأَنْفَالِ: properties reserved for the Imam, including certain lands and resources
key_terms.الْخُمُسِ: the one-fifth levy due on specified categories of wealth
key_terms.الْغَنَائِمُ: spoils or acquired gains subject to khums
key_terms.الْغَيْبَةِ: the period of occultation in which legal application is discussed
key_terms.الْفَوَائِدُ: benefits and profits obtained by a person

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith from al-Istibṣār say about khums on profits, gifts, inheritance, and property during the ghaybah?
ai.summary: This report records a letter from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام explaining a specific khums ruling for a particular year, while also clarifying the broader obligation of khums on gains and benefits. It distinguishes between categories of wealth, cites Qur'anic proof-texts, and shows a policy of easing burdens on the Shiʿah in light of political oppression and practical hardship.
